statement: For the continuous linear model ẋ(t) = A x(t) + B u(t) + w(t), where w is continuous white noise with power spectral density Q_c, sampling with period T gives x[k+1] = F x[k] + B_d u[k] + w[k] with w[k] ~ N(0, Q). Here F = e^{AT}, B_d = (∫_0^T e^{Aτ} dτ) B, and Q = ∫_0^T e^{Aτ} Q_c e^{Aᵀτ} dτ. Q can be computed from the exponential of the block matrix M = [[-A, Q_c],[0, Aᵀ]] T: if G = e^M = [[…, F⁻¹Q],[0, Fᵀ]], then Q = (G_22)ᵀ G_12. Renaming: the source writes A_d for the discrete transition matrix (here F), Q for the continuous noise spectral density (here Q_c), Q_d for the discrete process noise covariance (here Q), R_d / R for the discrete / continuous measurement noise (here R / R_c), and F for the block matrix (here M). Scope of the source: it derives the deterministic part (F and B_d) step by step, and it states the formula for Q and the block-exponential method for computing it. It does NOT derive the Q integral from the stochastic convolution of w(t). That step is stated here as given and is not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: discrete state transition matrix, e^{AT} (source: A_d)
continuous process noise covariance / power spectral density (source: Q)
discrete process noise covariance, Cov(w[k]) (source: Q_d)
continuous measurement noise spectral density (source: R)
discrete measurement noise covariance, R_c / T (source: R_d)
block matrix [[-A, Q_c],[0, Aᵀ]] T used to compute Q (source: F)

steps.text: Start from the continuous model ẋ(t) = A x(t) + B u(t). The matrix exponential satisfies d/dt e^{At} = A e^{At} = e^{At} A.
Premultiply by e^{-At}: e^{-At} ẋ(t) = e^{-At} A x(t) + e^{-At} B u(t). The left side minus the first right-hand term is a total derivative, so d/dt[e^{-At} x(t)] = e^{-At} B u(t).
Integrate from 0 to t: e^{-At} x(t) − x(0) = ∫_0^t e^{-Aτ} B u(τ) dτ, so x(t) = e^{At} x(0) + ∫_0^t e^{A(t−τ)} B u(τ) dτ. This is the exact continuous solution.
Define x[k] = x(kT). Write x[k+1] and split the integral at kT: x[k+1] = e^{AT}[e^{AkT} x(0) + ∫_0^{kT} e^{A(kT−τ)} B u(τ) dτ] + ∫_{kT}^{(k+1)T} e^{A(kT+T−τ)} B u(τ) dτ. The bracket is x[k].

Assume u is constant over the step (u(τ) = u[k]). Substitute v = kT + T − τ, so dτ = −dv and the limits go from T down to 0: x[k+1] = e^{AT} x[k] + (∫_0^T e^{Av} dv) B u[k]. Therefore F = e^{AT} and B_d = (∫_0^T e^{Aτ} dτ) B.
If A is nonsingular, the integral has a closed form: B_d = A⁻¹(F − I) B. If A is singular, expand e^{AT} = Σ_{k≥0} (AT)^k / k! and integrate term by term: B_d = (Σ_{k≥1} A^{k−1} T^k / k!) B.

With process noise added, the discrete model is x[k+1] = F x[k] + B_d u[k] + w[k] with w[k] ~ N(0, Q), where Q = ∫_0^T e^{Aτ} Q_c e^{Aᵀτ} dτ. The measurement noise becomes R = R_c / T, because the continuous measurement noise is defined by a power spectral density. The source states the Q integral without deriving it.
To compute Q numerically, form M = [[−A, Q_c],[0, Aᵀ]] T and take G = e^M = [[…, F⁻¹Q],[0, Fᵀ]].
Recover Q by multiplying the transpose of the lower-right block of G by the upper-right block: Q = (Fᵀ)ᵀ (F⁻¹Q) = F (F⁻¹Q).

Small-T approximations replace e^{AT}. Forward Euler uses e^{AT} ≈ I + AT, giving x[k+1] ≈ (I + AT) x[k] + T B u[k]. Backward Euler uses (I − AT)⁻¹. The bilinear (Tustin) transform uses (I + ½AT)(I − ½AT)⁻¹. These approximations have different stability properties; the bilinear transform preserves the instability of the continuous system.

assumptions.assumption: The continuous dynamics are linear and time-invariant (A, B constant over the step).
assumptions.breaks_when: The system is nonlinear or A varies within a step. Then e^{AT} is not the exact transition, and a linearization re-evaluated each step is needed.

assumptions.assumption: The input u is held constant over each sampling interval (zero-order hold).
assumptions.breaks_when: u varies inside [kT, (k+1)T). Then B_d u[k] no longer equals the true input integral.

assumptions.assumption: Process noise is continuous white Gaussian noise with spectral density Q_c, so its discrete counterpart is w[k] ~ N(0, Q).
assumptions.breaks_when: The noise is coloured or correlated across steps. Then Q from this integral misstates the per-step covariance, and the source gives no derivation that would show the dependence.

assumptions.assumption: Closed form B_d = A⁻¹(F − I)B requires A nonsingular.
assumptions.breaks_when: A is singular, for example a constant-velocity or integrator model. Use the series form instead.

assumptions.assumption: Euler / Tustin approximations assume a small T relative to the system's time constants.
assumptions.breaks_when: ‖AT‖ is not small. Then I + AT is a poor substitute for e^{AT}, and stability can change.

failure_modes.mode: Using Q_c directly as the discrete Q (or Q_c·T without the e^{Aτ} weighting)
failure_modes.signature: The filter is overconfident or underconfident, and the error depends on the sample rate: the tuning changes when T changes.
failure_modes.cause: Spectral density and per-step covariance are confused. Q must be integrated over the step through the dynamics.

failure_modes.signature: The measurement weighting is wrong by a factor that scales with the sample rate.
failure_modes.cause: The continuous measurement noise is a power spectral density, so R = R_c / T.

failure_modes.signature: Inf or NaN, or very large B_d entries, for nearly singular A.
failure_modes.cause: Inverting an ill-conditioned or singular A. The series form or the augmented-exponential trick avoids it.

failure_modes.signature: The discrete model diverges even though the continuous system is stable, typically at large T.
failure_modes.cause: I + AT does not preserve the continuous stability properties, so the approximations behave differently.

failure_modes.mode: Reading the wrong block of G = e^M
failure_modes.signature: Q is not symmetric, or is not positive semidefinite.
failure_modes.cause: Q is (G_22)ᵀ G_12. Using G_12 alone gives F⁻¹Q, not Q.

instantiation.why_here: Nothing in agrios_ws computes F = e^{AT} or the integral for Q itself. Both robot_localization EKF nodes, ekf_local and ekf_global, do the discretization step inside the library. The shown line in src/ekf.cpp:436 propagates the covariance as transfer_function_jacobian_ · P · transfer_function_jacobianᵀ and then adds delta_sec × process_noise_covariance. That added term is the sheet's Q = ∫_0^T e^{Aτ} Q_c e^{Aᵀτ} dτ with e^{Aτ} taken as the identity, which gives T·Q_c. So the matrix the project sets plays the role of Q_c, and the library scales it by elapsed time to get the per-step Q.

concrete.in_your_project: process_noise_covariance, a 15x15 matrix with these diagonal entries: X=0.05, Y=0.05, Z=0.06, Roll=0.03, Pitch=0.03, Yaw=0.06, Vx=0.025, Vy=0.025, Vz=0.04, Vroll=0.01, Vpitch=0.01, Vyaw=0.02, Ax=0.01, Ay=0.01, Az=0.015. All off-diagonal entries are zero. ekf_local and ekf_global set identical values.
delta_sec in src/ekf.cpp:436, the scalar that multiplies process_noise_covariance in the shown line.

The 15x15 term delta_sec * (*process_noise_covariance) added to the estimate covariance. It is diagonal because Q_c is diagonal and the shown line only scales it. The sheet's full integral would produce off-diagonal terms whenever A couples states, for example position and velocity.
transfer_function_jacobian_ in src/ekf.cpp:436, the 15x15 matrix applied on both sides of estimate_error_covariance_ before Q is added.

The twist covariance on /odom_cov, set by odom_cov_relay.py:12-16. It is a 6x6 matrix with vx=0.05, vy=0.05 and vyaw=0.02, and all other entries zero. Both EKFs read it as odom0 and fuse only Vx, Vy and Vyaw from it.

knobs.means: Sets Q_c. The shown line multiplies the whole matrix by delta_sec and adds it to the propagated covariance on each predict step. Every diagonal entry, from X through Az, therefore grows its state's variance in proportion to elapsed time. With zero off-diagonals, the added term is diagonal.
Same role as in ekf_local, with identical diagonal values. It is scaled by delta_sec and added after transfer_function_jacobian_ · P · transfer_function_jacobianᵀ.

instantiation.notation: The sheet's Q_c is set by the parameter process_noise_covariance, and the library adds delta_sec times it as the sheet's Q. The sheet's F is the library's transfer_function_jacobian_, and its T is delta_sec.
